outcomeNote: mishna rulings with a Beit Shammai / Beit Hillel dispute

segments.he: מַתְנִי' הַזָּב, וְהַזָּבָה, וְהַנִּדָּה, וְהַיּוֹלֶדֶת, וְהַמְּצוֹרָע שֶׁמֵּתוּ — מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא, עַד שֶׁיִּמּוֹק הַבָּשָׂר. נׇכְרִי שֶׁמֵּת — טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The corpses of «a zav, and a zava, and a menstruating woman, and a woman after childbirth, and a leper, who died, transmit ritual impurity by carrying» their corpses, «until the flesh decays.» With regard to the corpse of «a gentile who died,» although when alive he transmits impurity like a zav, once he dies he is «ritually pure» and is prevented «from transmitting impurity.»

segments.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים מֵתוֹת נִדּוֹת, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נִדָּה אֶלָּא שֶׁמֵּתָה נִדָּה.
segments.en: «Beit Shammai say:» The status of «all women» when they «die» is as though they were «menstruating women» at the time of death. Therefore, the garments that they were wearing before they died are impure and require immersion. «And Beit Hillel say: Only» a woman «who died» with the impurity of «a menstruating woman» has the status of «a menstruating woman» after death.

moves.summary: the impure dead transmit impurity by carrying until the flesh decays; a dead gentile is pure
only a woman who died a niddah is a niddah
moves.about: whether every woman who dies has the status of a menstruating woman, or only one who died while menstruating
